newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Pakistani stocks stagger after surge to fresh high.
newsitem.headline: Pakistani stocks stagger after surge to fresh high.

text.p: Pakistan's high-flying stock market staggered on Wednesday on profit-taking and analysts warned investors it was entering a consolidation phase after rising nearly 30 percent this month.
But analysts also said the market still had not exhausted its upside.

The Karachi Stock Exchange's 100-share price index ended down 50.64 points, or 2.51 percent, on Wednesday at 1,965.87, due largely to profit-taking following Tuesday's 5.44 percent surge to a 30-month high.
"The market is consolidating now," analyst Ali Raza Mooney of Kausar Abbas Bhayani Securities said.
But he said the market's rise should resume.
"Blue chips will rise further on expectations of good corporate results for the year ended June 30, 1997."
Ing Barings analyst Aliya Ehmar said: "We expect the market to continue its upward trend although a correction might be due in the short term."
Dealer Kamran Rizvi of Taurus Securities Ltd said: "Actively traded stocks should witness some decline in prices in the sessions ahead and investors in these shares should remain cautious."
But Rizvi added: "After a 28.8-percent rise so far this month, some technical correction is expected and profit-taking will be a healthy sign."
Tuesday's rally was fueled by huge foreign and local buying, luring other local investors into the market, KSE president Arif Habib said.
